diagnoses.bug: Decimal parsing uses i128 for the intermediate magnitude, so sufficiently long but syntactically valid decimals panic instead of returning DecimalOverflow.
diagnoses.lesson: Ensure every input length allowed by the specification follows a defined error path; avoid unchecked intermediate arithmetic that can panic on valid syntax.

diagnoses.bug: The parser checks the next quote byte for an escape without checking NUL first, so a quote followed by NUL is consumed as an escape and the reported error may be delayed or changed.
diagnoses.lesson: When lookahead consumes input, validate every consumed byte in the required order before changing parser state.

diagnoses.bug: Dependency evidence paths are built from data.paths before canonical paths are computed, so nested origins can omit their source path and fail to represent the required canonical incoming path.
diagnoses.lesson: Compute canonical graph paths before constructing derived provenance, and ensure every reported origin uses the finalized path to its source.

diagnoses.bug: The parser returns only the first local byte’s origin, so stripping a leading `+` reports that byte’s position instead of the plus’s original offset.
diagnoses.lesson: Track source offsets for every retained or transformed byte, and report errors using the specific byte that caused them.

diagnoses.bug: The function checks Old completely before checking New, so a missing final LF in Old masks a carriage return in New, contrary to the required validation precedence.
diagnoses.lesson: When requirements specify validation precedence, order checks by error category across all inputs before returning any error.

diagnoses.bug: The old-coordinate ordering check uses `< previous_old_end`, so it rejects same-anchor zero-length hunks when the previous hunk consumes no lines.
diagnoses.lesson: Translate ordering rules into explicit boundary cases, especially whether equality at an interval boundary is allowed.

diagnoses.bug: The pinned-feasibility check wrongly adds the replaced entry’s pinned weight back in, so valid same-key replacements can return Blocked.
diagnoses.lesson: When replacing an existing item, exclude its old state consistently from feasibility checks and accounting before validating the proposed state.

diagnoses.bug: resolve_links initializes its traversal stack from cwd or home without looking up links on those components, so links encountered in the starting directory are skipped.
diagnoses.lesson: Apply event-driven rules consistently to every item in the processing sequence, including elements supplied by an initial context.

diagnoses.bug: When several jobs become Blocked in one propagation pass, the code mutates their states before choosing skip dependencies, so a job may cite a newly Blocked dependent instead of its original Failed dependency.
diagnoses.lesson: Preserve causal information before mutating a batch of related states, then derive emitted records from that snapshot.

diagnoses.bug: The shortest-route tie-break chooses the smallest next component ID greedily, which does not always produce the lexicographically smallest complete route among equal-length paths.
diagnoses.lesson: For lexicographic path ties, compare complete candidate paths; a locally smallest next step may not yield the globally smallest route.

diagnoses.bug: `intersects` infers overlap from endpoints and a few anchors, so it misses valid interior prerelease witnesses and discrete adjacency cases.
diagnoses.lesson: For existence checks over ordered domains, reason about interval bounds and successor structure instead of sampling endpoints or a few representative values.

diagnoses.bug: restore and forget validate only empty snapshot names, so invalid nonempty names can incorrectly return SnapshotMissing or succeed instead of NameInvalid at the first offending byte.
diagnoses.lesson: Apply every specified input-validation rule consistently across all operations that accept the same input type, before lookup or mutation.

diagnoses.bug: When userinfo is present, its validation base offset is set to the authority start instead of the byte immediately after the `@`, so reported escape and UTF-8 offsets are too early.
diagnoses.lesson: Track each parsed field’s original byte range and use its true start when translating nested validation errors.

diagnoses.bug: Ordinary relative references are assembled with the normalized base path before parsing, so parse errors report offsets in that modified URL instead of the required constructed raw URL.
diagnoses.lesson: Preserve the specified intermediate representation through validation; normalization before parsing can change both behavior and error offsets.

diagnoses.bug: decode_many calls Vec::with_capacity(count) before decoding, so a huge count can panic or abort instead of returning a result.
diagnoses.lesson: Validate input-driven allocation sizes and avoid reserving unbounded capacity before establishing that the requested work is feasible.

diagnoses.bug: decode_many uses Vec::with_capacity(count), so a huge count can trigger capacity overflow or allocation failure before decoding and panic on a small input.
diagnoses.lesson: Validate and bound resource use from caller-controlled sizes before allocating; ensure error paths remain safe for extreme inputs.

lessons: Validate caller-controlled sizes and bound resource use before allocating or doing work; keep extreme-input error paths safe.
Apply every specified validation rule consistently across all operations that accept the same input, before lookup or mutation.
Honor validation precedence across all inputs: check error categories in the specified order before returning an error.
Track original byte ranges through parsing and transformation; report errors at the byte that caused them, without normalizing before validation.
Check every consumed byte in the required order before changing parser state, and define safe error paths for all valid input lengths.
Preserve causal state before mutating related items, then derive outputs from that snapshot; exclude replaced state consistently from feasibility checks and accounting.
Compute finalized canonical paths before deriving provenance, and compare complete candidate paths when resolving lexicographic ties.
Translate ordering rules into explicit boundary cases, and reason about ordered-domain intervals and successors rather than sampling representative values.
